takeaway: Ejection fraction is the ratio of stroke volume to end-diastolic volume.

question.text: A patient with a 6 cm abdominal aortic aneurysm has an echocardiogram before elective repair. The ejection fraction is defined as what?
question.say: A patient with a six centimetre abdominal aortic aneurysm is scheduled for elective repair, and an echocardiogram is requested. The ejection fraction is defined as what?

answer.text: The ratio of stroke volume to end-diastolic volume
answer.say: The answer is the ratio of stroke volume to end-diastolic volume.

lines.text: Our patient has a 6 cm aneurysm.
lines.say: Our smiling patient has a six centimetre aortic aneurysm, waiting for elective repair.

lines.text: The echocardiogram checks the heart first.
lines.say: Before surgery, the echocardiogram checks how well his heart pumps.

lines.text: The full bucket: end-diastolic volume, about 120 mL.
lines.say: In diastole the ventricle fills to about one hundred and twenty millilitres. This full bucket is the end-diastolic volume.

lines.text: The cup: stroke volume, about 70 mL.
lines.say: In systole the heart pours out about seventy millilitres into the cup. That is the stroke volume.

lines.text: Ejection fraction = stroke volume / end-diastolic volume.
lines.say: (laugh) So the ejection fraction is simply the cup divided by the bucket.

lines.text: Remember: EF is stroke volume over end-diastolic volume.
lines.say: Remember: ejection fraction is the ratio of stroke volume to end-diastolic volume.
